Repair and extend the offline residential IPv6 campaign toolkit.
The multi-file Python workspace is in `/workspace/submission`.
Its generator, compressed capture classifier and device protocol adapters
must support the campaign interface specified in `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
Implement revision-aware evidence reconciliation across prefix leases,
a causal service census, and an optimal quota-constrained follow-up plan.
Return the target manifest, rejected-record indices, snapshot reports,
request activity, and a checkable probe-script certificate.
All input addresses are documentation addresses; never contact targets.
Read `/workspace/SYSCALLS.md` for the exact child and checker-parent profiles.
Pinned dependencies are bundled; runtime and checks require no network.
Submit the entire `/workspace/submission` directory, with `campaign.py`
as its entry point. You may change, add or reorganize ordinary files.
The entry point receives one UTF-8 JSON object on stdin and writes one
UTF-8 JSON object on stdout. Other output belongs on stderr.
Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/submission` for sanity checks.
The public examples cover only a small part of the stated domain.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of the work:

## Implemented revision-aware offline campaign toolkit

**`common.py`** â metadata envelope validation: exact root/record keys, ID syntax, integer-only JSON (booleans/floats/nonfinite rejected, BOM/duplicate keys/trailing data invalid), strict documentation-range address/prefix parsing, base64, and quota-forest validation (no cycles, â¤32 node paths).

**`gen_targets.py`** â deterministic canary/low-IID manifest (`SHA256(seed\nlease\ncanonical_/64)[:8] | 2â¶Â³`) in lexical-lease â numeric-subnet â canary-then-IID order, with a numeric probe lookup table.

**`classify_responses.py`** â in-memory capture transport: base64 chunk decoding with a 32 MiB budget, complete dictionary-free Zstandard framing validation (skippable/concatenated frames, unused bit ignored, reserved bit/window/dictionary/truncation/checksum/content-size rejected), strict Excel CSV streaming with 128 MiB decompressed/200 000 record/131 072 byte bounds, plus the per-lease role/witness reconciliation.

**`ledger.py`** â 14-field typed record parsing (delete/put, ICMP vs application field rules, probe/target numerical matching, payload bounds) and `(type,id)` reconciliation: highest visible revision wins, identical semantic contents collapse (publication time, address/decimal/base64 spelling ignored), conflicting contents contribute nothing.

**`census.py`** â snapshots in query order: `inactive/alias/conflict/usable` states, raw conflicts even when alias wins, clean I/E with causal witnesses, unresolved low targets, the causal application census (latest-attempt arbitration, signature agreement, per-identity protocol errors), `internal_only`, and frozen request activity.

**`protocols.py`** â repaired ADB (length/checksum/magic/trailing validation, CNXN version triple, AUTH) and usbmuxd sync (two length-prefixed plists, exact keys, strict UTF-8) plus the probe certificate packets.

**`planning.py`** â optimal quota-constrained plan as a min-cost maximum flow: source down the request quota forest, one pair edge, up the offer quota forest, sink â which makes integral flows exactly correspond to feasible assignments. Interchangeable requests and duplicate offers are merged, non-binding quota nodes contracted, and a Dijkstra+potentials/blocking-flow SSP produces the maximum-cardinality, minimum-cost certificate.

Validated by 12 local suites, ~7 000 randomized comparisons against an independently written reference implementation, and brute-force plan oracles (this caught two real bugs, including a residual-arc issue that silently broke rerouting).
